neighbours.label: end of an opinion or concession clause in argumentative first-person prose (I love wind power. / I'm not saying X shouldn't be funded.)
fire: Let me be clear about three things. I support public transport. Buses, trams, all of it.
I'm not trying to say that the library shouldn't be funded. I'm saying it's one priority among many.
It is absurd to suggest that no report should ever be kept secret. Would that really be wise?
I love solar panels. Small ones, big ones, on every roof I can find.
Nobody here is claiming that teachers are overpaid. We are asking where the money goes.
I have nothing against cyclists. I just want the paths to be safe for walkers too.
To be honest, I think the plan is a good one. It just needs more time.
I'm sure that if I buy an umbrella today, it will never rain again.
quiet: The council met on Tuesday to review the bus timetable for the coming year.
The library opens at nine and closes at six on weekdays.
The report was filed in March and reviewed by two departments.
Solar panels convert sunlight into electricity using silicon cells.
Teachers in the district start the school year in late August.
The cycle path runs along the river for about twelve kilometres.
The plan was approved by the board after a short meeting.
The forecast for tomorrow shows light rain in the morning.
